To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the $N^*$-induced production of antiprotons is important, but the $N^{*$}$-induced production contributions of kaons and antikaons are small.

the contribution of the N* resonance to the yield of subthreshold particles is strongly dependent on the in-medium properties of the N* and the antiproton, and that a significant fraction of the subthreshold particle yield is generated by N* resonance interactions.

the $N^{+}$ resonance contributes about 10\% (25\%) to the total kaon (antikaon) yield, about 80\% of the antiprotons originate from the $N^{*-}$ resonance, and the contribution from the $N^*$-baryon interaction decreases (increases) by a factor of about 3 (35) if the resonance widths are increased (the antiproton production thresholds are decreased) in the nuclear medium.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of the $N^*(1440)$ resonance in heavy-ion collisions.
the effects of $p$-$p$ collisions on the production of antiprotons, kaons, and anti-kaons in heavy-ion collisions.

the production of kaon and antikaon in the reaction $NN \rightarrow N\bar{K}N$ and antiproton in the reactions $NN \rightarrow \bar{K}NN$, $N\bar{K}\rightarrow \bar{N}N$ and $\bar{K} \bar{K}\to N \bar{N}$ at subthreshold energies and the effects of the $\Delta$ and the $N^*$ resonance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the $N^*(1440)$ resonance is an important source of subthreshold antiproton production, and that the $N*(1440)$ induced collisions contribute about 10-80\% to total kaon, antiproton and antikaon yields.
the $N^*$-resonance effects are significant and cannot be neglected in heavy-ion collisions.
$N^{*}$(1400) resonance plays a significant role in the subthreshold production of kaons and antiproton.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effects of $pN^{*}(1400)$ interactions on antiproton production are significant at subthreshold energies.
the $N^*$-baryon resonance plays a very significant role in the production of antiprotons and antikaons in heavy-ion collisions, but its effect on kaon production is not so important.

the $N^*$-baryon collisions are an important source for the subthreshold antiproton production and that a proper treatment of the $N^*-N^{*-}$ collisions and of the in-medium thresholds is necessary for a quantitative description of the antiproton yield.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the $N(1440)$ resonance can play an important role in the subthreshold production of kaons and antiproton and the effect of the resonance can be significantly modified due to in-medium changes in the resonance properties and the production thresholds.
the $N^{\ast}$-baryons are important for subthreshold antiproton production in heavy-ion collisions.
$N^{*}$(1430) resonance plays a significant role in antiproton production and the antiproton production mechanism is very sensitive to in-medium effects.
